question.problem: Find a point that satisfies the mean value theorem for $f(x,y)=3{y}^{2}+xy+2{x}^{2}$ on the line segment $\overset{―}{AB},$ where the position vectors of $A$ and $B$ are $a=⟨0,3⟩$ and $b=⟨3,4⟩,$ respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The mean value theorem states that if $f(x,y)$ is differentiable at each point on the line segment $\overset{―}{AB},$ then there exists a point $C\in \overset{―}{AB}$ with position vector $c$ such that

$$
f(b)-f(a)=∇f(c)·(b-a).
$$

Notice that the function $f(x,y)=3{y}^{2}+xy+2{x}^{2}$ is differentiable at each point on the line segment $\overset{―}{AB}.$ So, we can apply the mean value theorem.

Substituting $a=⟨0,3⟩$ and $b=⟨3,4⟩$ into the above expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3,4)-f(0,3) & =∇f(c)\cdot (⟨3,4⟩-⟨0,3⟩) \\ 3(4)^{2}+3(4)+2(3)^{2}-(3(3)^{2}+0(3)+2(0)^{2}) & =∇f(c)\cdot ⟨3,1⟩ \\ 51 & =∇f(c)\cdot ⟨3,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $∇f$ and evaluating at $c=⟨{c}_{1},{c}_{2}⟩,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨4x+y,x+6y⟩, \\ ∇f(c) & =⟨4{c}_{1}+{c}_{2},{c}_{1}+6{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}51 & =∇f⟨c⟩\cdot ⟨3,1⟩ \\ 51 & =⟨4{c}_{1}+{c}_{2},{c}_{1}+6{c}_{2}⟩\cdot ⟨3,1⟩ \\ 51 & =12{c}_{1}+3{c}_{2}+{c}_{1}+6{c}_{2} \\ 51 & =13{c}_{1}+9{c}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $C$ lies on $\overset{―}{AB}.$ So, let's first find the equation of the line.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y-{y}_{a}}{{y}_{b}-{y}_{a}} & =\frac{x-{x}_{a}}{{x}_{b}-{x}_{a}} \\ \frac{y-3}{4-3} & =\frac{x-0}{3-0} \\ y-3 & =\frac{x}{3} \\ y & =\frac{x}{3}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $c=⟨{c}_{1},{c}_{2}⟩$ satisfies the equation of the line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{2} & =\frac{{c}_{1}}{3}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the equation $13{c}_{1}+9{c}_{2}=51,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}13{c}_{1}+9(\frac{{c}_{1}}{3}+3) & =51 \\ 13{c}_{1}+3{c}_{1}+27 & =51 \\ 16{c}_{1} & =24 \\ {c}_{1} & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${c}_{2}=\frac{{c}_{1}}{3}+3=\frac{7}{2}.$ So, the point $C$ that satisfies the mean value theorem is $(\frac{3}{2},\frac{7}{2}).$
